name: D1 Visa (Subordinate Work)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a signed employment contract or promise of contract for subordinate work of more than 12 months with a Portuguese employer.
This requires a salary of at least €920/month gross (the 2026 minimum wage).
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a higher salary or confirm the offer meets the current minimum wage.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a favourable labour-market opinion from IEFP (the Portuguese employment agency), and — from mid-2026 — consular pre-authorization of the contract before booking a visa appointment.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract or promise of contract
Consular contract pre-authorization/homologation code (new process from mid-2026)

sources.title: AIMA — D1 residence visa for subordinate work

notes: Portugal's direct equivalent to UK Skilled Worker, Germany's general skilled-worker permits, and NL Highly Skilled Migrant — the standard employer-sponsored route. GENUINE PROCESS CHANGE confirmed for 2026, not present in earlier research on this route: from mid-2026 a new consular pre-authorization step was added, requiring the employer to validate the contract with the consulate (obtaining a homologation code) BEFORE the worker can book a VFS Global appointment — this materially changes the practical sequence of the application compared to how the route worked even a year earlier, and is exactly the kind of process detail that goes stale fast on secondary sites. Salary floor is the flat RMMG (€920/month) with no occupation-specific 'going rate' table of the kind UK Skilled Worker uses — a genuine structural simplicity relative to UK's LookupTable-requiring salary system, worth surfacing in a cross-country comparison. family_can_join is subject to the same 2-year residence wait as pt_family_reunification generally, with exceptions for minor children — not re-stated as a separate conditional here to avoid duplicating that route's more detailed handling.
